sections.h2: Selling a house in Apple Valley
sections.html:
Apple Valley lies in northwestern Dakota County, so a sale involves the county's recording and tax offices in Hastings plus a few city rules on signs, parking and rentals. The paperwork looks much the same whichever way you sell.

Owners of homes that need work, carry unpaid tax or have tenants sometimes ask for cash offers, since the buyer takes the property as it stands. The Dakota County Community Development Agency also coordinates foreclosure assistance and home rehabilitation programs for Apple Valley, which is worth a call before you decide.

Apple Valley is mature and mostly built out. It has 55,248 residents, 2.0 percent fewer than the 56,374 counted in 2020, because the city has nearly used up its buildable land. The typical owner-occupied home was worth $370,400 for 2020 to 2024, and 73.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Median owner cost with a mortgage is $2,084 a month, median gross rent is $1,738, and households average 2.55 people. With little new land, resale houses make up most of what buyers see.

sections.h2: City rules a seller should know
sections.html:
Short term rentals of fewer than 30 days are not allowed in Apple Valley. A council ordinance clarified that they have never been a permitted use, so a house marketed to investors as an Airbnb or Vrbo property will not work as advertised. Owners of any residential rental property must register it with the city.

Yard and curb rules also come up during showings and open houses:

  • One for-sale sign per frontage, two on a corner lot, kept inside the property line and off the right of way, which usually reaches 13 feet behind the curb.
  • Open house signs may stand on city right of way within six blocks of the house, only on the day and during the hours of the open house.
  • Grass and weeds taller than eight inches are a public nuisance.
  • No more than four vehicles per home may be parked or stored outside, and all parking areas must be paved with concrete, asphalt or pavers.
  • Lawn watering is barred from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. between May 1 and September 30, and public sidewalks must be cleared within 48 hours after a snowfall ends.

Trash containers go to the curb no earlier than 6 p.m. the night before pickup and come back by 10 p.m. on collection day. A garage sale may run three consecutive days, three times a year. Sheds of 200 square feet or less need no building permit, and fences over seven feet do. Code Enforcement at 952-953-2570 answers questions, and the Planning Department at 952-953-2575 handles setbacks.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Dakota County
sections.html:
Deeds, mortgages and liens for every parcel are held by Dakota County Property Taxation and Records. Walk-in recording happens at the Administration Center, 1590 Highway 55 in Hastings, and requires an appointment. Mailed packets need the fees, a cover letter, a return envelope with postage and a phone number.

Land in Minnesota is recorded under two systems. With Abstract property, a title company searches the chain of documents. Torrens property instead carries a single certificate of title, close to final proof of who owns it. Abstract is the norm in Dakota County.

Wells matter at the recorder's counter. A transfer deed, a deed ending a contract for deed included, must come with a well disclosure certificate and a $54 fee unless the deed itself carries a statement. The statement can say the seller is unaware of any wells, or that the wells' number and status are unchanged from the last certificate on file. Staff do not assist with legal forms, so let the title company or an attorney prepare the paperwork.

sections.h2: How to pay Dakota County property tax
sections.html:
Real property tax is due May 15 and October 15, and the owner is responsible for timely payment whatever method is used. Manufactured homes follow August 31 and November 15, and farm second halves land on November 15.

Single online payments run through Paymentus, with a $100,000 ceiling per transaction, and you are done only when an emailed receipt shows up. Alternatives include the phone line at 1-844-797-9075, a mailed check to 1590 Highway 55, Hastings, MN 55033-2343 postmarked by the deadline, or a weekday visit to the Western Service Center in Apple Valley. The Hastings and West St. Paul offices also accept payments.

Free automatic withdrawals are open to owners without a mortgage-company escrow and without overdue tax. Cancellations need 15 days' notice before a due date. Statement and payoff questions go to 651-438-4576 or taxation@co.dakota.mn.us.

sections.h2: Before you list or accept a cash offer
sections.html:
Start with three calls. Ask Dakota County taxation at 651-438-4576 for the payoff on any unpaid tax. Call Code Enforcement at 952-953-2570 to learn whether any yard or parking issue is open on the property. If tenants live there, make sure the rental is registered with the city. Then give the title company or an attorney the well information so the deed can carry the right statement or certificate.

A cash buyer skips the lender, so the sale can move as quickly as the paperwork does. That means the tax payoff, the well statement and the recording appointment decide your closing date, and booking the recording appointment early removes the most common delay.

sections.h2: What to expect between offer and closing
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, the title company searches the chain of documents, which is the Abstract route used for most Dakota County parcels. It also requests the tax figures and reviews the deed for the well statement. You sign the deed and the disclosure paperwork at closing, and the title company then takes the deed to Property Taxation and Records for recording. Staff there do not help with legal forms, so any questions about wording go to the title company or an attorney.

If a buyer plans to rent the house, remind them that Apple Valley bars stays of fewer than 30 days and that any residential rental must be registered with the city. If the house is staying a rental under the new owner, give the buyer your tenant and registration details at the start. A buyer who pays cash will still want the same answers, and having them ready keeps the closing date from slipping. Check yard and parking items one more time before the final walkthrough, because a fresh notice from Code Enforcement can complicate a closing that is otherwise ready.

faqs.q: Can I run an Airbnb in Apple Valley, MN?
faqs.a: No. Rentals under 30 days are barred, and the council's ordinance says they were never allowed. Longer-term rentals must be registered with the city.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for an Apple Valley house?
faqs.a: Property Taxation and Records at the Dakota County Administration Center, 1590 Highway 55, Hastings. Appointments are available online, and mail recording is accepted.

faqs.q: What is a well disclosure certificate in Dakota County?
faqs.a: A filing that goes with each transfer deed for $54. A statement on the deed about unknown or unchanged wells can stand in for it.

faqs.q: How many cars can I park outside an Apple Valley home?
faqs.a: No more than four vehicles per dwelling unit, on a paved surface. An annual on-site parking permit allows two more, and the Planning Department at 952-953-2575 takes applications.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Apple Valley?
faqs.a: Independent School District 196. Some families opt into other districts under Minnesota's open enrollment statute.
